properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 10:12AM AST until November 25 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline,
from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S.
Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St.
Thomas, St. John and adjacent islands.

* WHEN...Through 6 PM AST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 25 at 4:10AM HST until November 26 at 8:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI

...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI MAUI...NORTH FACING SHORES OF BIG
ISLAND...AND EAST FACING SHORES OF KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI MAUI AND
BIG ISLAND...
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR WEST FACING SHORES OF BIG
ISLAND...
...COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT IN EFFECT FOR ALL HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...

.A large, long-period north-northwest swell will fade today,
causing surf along north and west-facing shores to fall below
warning level briefly today. An even larger north-northwest swell
arrives this afternoon into tonight, peaking overnight into
Thursday well above warning level. Surf could remain above
warning level into Friday. Higher than predicted water levels
could lead to flooding of beaches that typically remain dry,
particularly during the pre-dawn high tides this morning and

ramps and other coastal infrastructure of all Hawaiian islands.

* WHEN...Through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of beaches that are normally dry, minor

properties.instruction:

drive through salt water, be sure to rinse your vehicle with
fresh water. Move electronics, vehicles or other valuables to
higher ground. Monitor vessels to ensure mooring lines don't get
too tight and watch out for overwash around boat ramps. Secure
canoes or other watercraft stowed on beaches.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 8:07AM CST until November 25 at 9:30AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 930 AM CST.

* At 806 AM CST, strong thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 24 nm south of
Farewell Buoy to 56 nm south of Sand Island Lighthouse, moving east
at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to 40 knots, and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Strong thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 6:02AM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides,
combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave
heights of 20 to 25 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of
inundation above ground level today, with up to 2.6 ft of
inundation expected on Thursday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the
communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold
Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact
portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and
Reedsport.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the high tide periods in the late morning/early
afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides
will still be present, which will likely continue inundation
impacts. At the Charleston, Oregon tide gauge, high tide is
expected to be at 11:35 AM today, at 12:23 PM Thursday, and at
1:14 PM Friday. Tides look to return to more typical heights
over the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 25 at 5:53AM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of
20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, through midnight PST
Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at
10:49 AM Wednesday and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 4:50AM PST until November 25 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas. Up to 1 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf
may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood
Coast. Up to 1.0 foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves up
to 25 feet. Surf may worsen coastal flooding along exposed
beaches.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM to 7 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Thursday morning
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to sections of
Highways 101 and 1. Shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected
to rival the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant coastal impacts.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 3:10AM PST until November 25 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along
the coast. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground
level is possible Wednesday along shorelines and low-lying
coastal areas. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 3 to
4 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM PST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday
night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash
over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 12 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level expected
in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM Wednesday to 10
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 PM
Wednesday to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways resulting in a elevated threat of property damage.
Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening
some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding
of vehicles will be possible. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...By Wednesday morning minor to locally
moderate impacts will be possible prior to the start of
warning level criteria with the greatest impacts being felt
Thursday morning. As winds switch to a SW direction Thursday
afternoon, minor water level rises (around 1-2 ft) on
soundside locations will be possible.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Washington; Tyrrell
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 4:59AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 3 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along the Albemarle Sound and Scuppernong River,
and adjacent tidal creeks.

* WHEN...From 7 PM Wednesday to 4 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The King Tides will be exacerbated by a
strong coastal low that will impact the area Wednesday into
Thursday. Strong easterly winds ahead of the low will bring
elevated waters levels on the western portion of the Albemarle
Sound with the worst impacts are currently forecast with the
morning high tide cycle on Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Metro Palm Beach County; Metro Broward County; Metropolitan Miami Dade; Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 4:58AM EST until November 26 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 1:51AM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of
flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with
peak tides trending from 8 AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak each day through Thursday
at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. A long period west swell arrives late
this afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by Thursday
morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 4-6 feet with
local sets up to 7-8 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to
3-5 feet by Friday morning's high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Nassau
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 25 at 4:21AM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 foot of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, 2 to 3, locally 3 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level
expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Watch, up to 2 to 3 ft of
inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Nassau County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST this
morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to
6 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major
flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront.
Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become
flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront
along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result
in widespread beach flooding and dune erosion widespread beach
flooding and dune erosion during times of high tide. There is
potential for localized overwashes resulting in some flooding
of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday morning high tides. This forecast will
be refined over the next 12 to 24 hours as timing of wind
forcing with respect to Thursday AM/PM high tides becomes more
clear. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water
level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing
of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak
water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for
Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could
be lowered slightly.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

sharp cutoff appears likely to setup within 25 miles of the

heavier axis.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 3 PM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning
commutes.
properties.instruction:

can be obtained by visiting www.weather.gov/pah/roads

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 24 at 8:15PM PST until November 29 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall
to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow
levels rising as high as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The
combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels is
expected to push the Skokomish River near Potlach above flood
stage by midweek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 24 at 5:51PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15
to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 24 at 5:51PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
Localized moderate to significant coastal flooding is expected
for Jalama Beach and for most coastal areas from Miramar Beach
to Rincon Point. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Conditions
will be worse west of Point Conception, including Jalama Beach
with large breaking waves of 15 to 20 feet and moderate to
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 AM Wednesday to
noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and
seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greater impacts are expected west of Point
Conception, and for most coastal areas from Miramar Beach to
Rincon Point, where damaging flooding of sea water is more
likely, especially for vulnerable low-lying coastal areas
around the time of high tide including over beaches, beach
parking lots and coastal roads. For the previously mentioned
areas, significant beach erosion is expected, powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures and homes at the
waters edge. Extremely high tides of 8.0-8.4 feet will likely
peak between 7am and 11am.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high

properties.description:

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.

local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.

11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5
ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW
(7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27.

11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3
ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW
(6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,

properties.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures in the mid to upper 20s expected.

* WHERE...All of west central Texas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
properties.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means sub-freezing temperatures are imminent or
highly likely. These conditions will kill crops and other sensitive
vegetation.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold. To prevent
freezing and possible bursting of outdoor water pipes they should be
wrapped, drained, or allowed to drip slowly. Those that have
in-ground sprinkler systems should drain them and cover above-ground
pipes to protect them from freezing.

amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with localized higher totals of
3 to 4 inches possible.

possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including, Indian River,
Martin, Saint Lucie, Brevard, and Okeechobee counties.

* WHEN...From 1 AM EST Wednesday through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

higher amounts of 3 to 4 inches will be possible. Heavy rainfall
over saturated soils may lead to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 1:10PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday Nov 30.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 110 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
